related_questions.question: Why are US markets closed on June 19?

text_blocks.snippet: US stock and bond markets are closed on Thursday, June 19, 2025, in observance of Juneteenth National Independence Day. This is a federal holiday commemorating the emancipation of enslaved African Americans. Both the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and Nasdaq will be closed for the day and will resume trading on Friday, June 20.

Juneteenth became a federal holiday in 2021, and since then, the stock market has observed it as a full-day closure. This means that not only stocks but also options, and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) will not be traded on June 19. The bond market will also be closed.

related_questions.question: Should a 70 year old get out of the stock market?
related_questions.snippet: As a general statement, though, you probably wouldn't want any more than 30% of your assets in stocks after age 70 or so. Your tolerance for risk should naturally decline with time, since you're less concerned about return on investment and more concerned about maintain financial solvency. Good luck to you!

related_questions.snippet: Understanding the Rule of 90 The Rule of 90 is a grim statistic that serves as a sobering reminder of the difficulty of trading.
